SOAP Note

Subjective:

64 y/o male presents with chief complaint of lower back pain x 3 months. Reports pain is 6/10 at rest, 8/10 with bending forward and prolonged standing. Pain occasionally radiates down right leg to knee level. Denies numbness, tingling, or weakness in lower extremities. Reports difficulty with activities such as gardening, playing with grandchildren, and sitting >30 minutes. Previous treatments include over-the-counter NSAIDs with minimal relief. No red flag symptoms reported. Patient is motivated to return to previous activity level and avoid surgical intervention.

Objective:

Observation: Antalgic gait with decreased step length on right. Increased lumbar lordosis. Forward head posture noted.

ROM: Lumbar flexion 65° (limited, normal ~80°), extension 18° (limited, normal ~25°). Right hip: flexion 105° (limited), extension 12° (limited), abduction 28° (restricted). Left hip within normal limits.

Strength (MMT): Hip flexors 4/5 bilaterally. Right hip abductors 3/5 (weak), left 4+/5. Core musculature demonstrates poor endurance with plank test (15 seconds).

Special Tests: Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. FABER test positive on right (reproduces anterior hip/groin discomfort). Posterior hip provocation tests negative.

Functional Assessment: Squat pattern shows excessive trunk lean and limited depth due to hip/lumbar restrictions. Single leg stance: Left 24.3 sec (adequate), Right 18.1 sec (below average) with increased postural sway. Gait analysis reveals decreased right hip extension in terminal stance phase.

Assessment:

Primary Diagnosis: Lumbar facet dysfunction with associated right hip weakness and movement pattern dysfunction.

Contributing Factors: Right hip flexor and capsular tightness, bilateral hip abductor weakness (R>L), core stabilization deficits, age-related changes, BMI 27.9 (overweight).

Prognosis: Good. Patient demonstrates high motivation and no significant comorbidities that would impede progress. Expected to achieve 70-80% improvement in 6-8 weeks with consistent adherence to prescribed exercise program.

Injury Risk Level: MODERATE-HIGH (68/100). Primary risk factors include balance asymmetry, hip weakness, and lumbar ROM limitations. Fall risk assessment indicates need for balance training.

Plan:

Frequency: 2x/week for 6-8 weeks, with home exercise program (HEP) daily.

Treatment Approach:

  • Manual therapy: Lumbar mobilizations grade III-IV, right hip joint mobilizations
  • Soft tissue work: Right hip flexor/TFL release, lumbar paraspinal work
  • Therapeutic exercise: Core stabilization progression, hip strengthening (focus abductors), balance training, functional movement re-education
  • Patient education: Posture correction, body mechanics, pain management strategies
  • Modalities as needed: Heat for muscle relaxation, ice for post-exercise inflammation management

Short-term Goals (2-3 weeks): Reduce pain to 3-4/10, increase lumbar flexion to 75°, improve right hip abduction strength to 4/5, single leg stance >20 sec bilaterally.

Long-term Goals (6-8 weeks): Pain 0-2/10 with all ADLs, return to gardening and grandchild care activities, normalize movement patterns, independent with HEP for long-term management.

Home Exercise Program (HEP)

1 Pelvic Tilts

Core Stability Beginner

Sets: 3 | Reps: 15 | Frequency: Daily

Purpose: Improve core control and lumbar mobility

View Instructions
  1. Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat
  2. Tighten abdominal muscles
  3. Tilt pelvis upward, flattening lower back against floor
  4. Hold 5 seconds, then relax
  5. Breathe normally throughout

2 Clamshells

Hip Strength Beginner

Sets: 3 | Reps: 12 each side | Frequency: Daily

Purpose: Strengthen hip abductors (gluteus medius)

Focus on RIGHT side - Add resistance band when ready

View Instructions
  1. Lie on side with hips and knees bent
  2. Keep feet together
  3. Lift top knee while keeping feet touching
  4. Hold 2 seconds at top
  5. Lower slowly, repeat

3 Bird Dogs

Core Stability Intermediate

Sets: 3 | Reps: 10 each side | Frequency: Daily

Purpose: Core stability and spinal control

View Instructions
  1. Start on hands and knees
  2. Extend right arm forward and left leg back
  3. Keep back straight, don't arch or sag
  4. Hold 5 seconds
  5. Return to start, switch sides

4 Single Leg Stance

Balance Beginner

Sets: 3 | Duration: 30 sec each leg | Frequency: Daily

Purpose: Improve balance and proprioception

EXTRA focus on RIGHT leg - Use chair for safety

View Instructions
  1. Stand next to chair or counter for safety
  2. Lift one foot off ground
  3. Balance on standing leg for 30 seconds
  4. Progress: Close eyes when able
  5. Switch legs

Important Instructions:

  • Perform exercises 1x daily, preferably same time each day
  • STOP immediately if sharp pain occurs - mild muscle soreness is normal
  • Warm up with 5 minutes of walking before exercises
  • Ice lower back for 15 min if soreness after exercises
  • Track completion in patient portal daily
  • Contact Dr. Johnson if pain increases or new symptoms develop

Movement Deficiency Analysis

🚨 Critical: Right Hip Abductor Weakness

Impact: Compensatory gait pattern, increased fall risk, lateral pelvic tilt during gait

Evidence:

  • MMT: Right 3/5 vs Left 4+/5
  • Single leg stance 25% worse on right
  • Hip abduction ROM restricted to 28° (normal 45°)

Exercises Targeting: Clamshells, Side-lying leg lifts, Single leg stance

⚠️ Moderate: Core Stabilization Deficit

Impact: Excessive trunk lean during squats, difficulty with prolonged sitting/standing

Evidence:

  • Plank test: Only 15 seconds (target >60 sec)
  • Squat shows 15° forward lean (compensatory)
  • Antalgic gait pattern observed

Exercises Targeting: Pelvic tilts, Bird dogs, Dead bugs, Planks (progression)

⚠️ Moderate: Lumbar ROM Limitation

Impact: Difficulty bending, compensatory hip movement, increased injury risk

Evidence:

  • Flexion: 65° (normal ~80°) - 19% deficit
  • Extension: 18° (normal ~25°) - 28% deficit
  • Patient reports difficulty with bending tasks

Treatment: Manual therapy, Cat-cow stretches, Knee-to-chest stretches

ℹ️ Mild: Right Hip Flexor Tightness

Impact: Contributes to anterior pelvic tilt, affects squat depth

Evidence:

  • Hip flexion 105° (limited compared to left 118°)
  • Extension limited to 12° (normal 15-20°)
  • FABER test positive on right

Treatment: Hip flexor stretching, Manual therapy, Foam rolling

Injury Risk Predictions

Based on assessment findings, the following injuries have elevated risk if deficiencies are not addressed:

Lower Back Strain / Disc Injury

HIGH RISK

Probability: 65% in next 6 months without intervention

Risk Factors:

  • Limited lumbar ROM + compensatory movement patterns
  • Core weakness unable to protect spine
  • Age-related disc degeneration risk
  • BMI 27.9 increases spinal loading

Prevention: Core strengthening program, proper body mechanics education, weight management, continue PT exercises

Fall / Hip Fracture

MODERATE RISK

Probability: 35% risk of fall in next 12 months

Risk Factors:

  • Right leg balance deficit (25% worse than left)
  • Age >60 with multiple comorbidities
  • Hip weakness contributing to instability
  • Antalgic gait pattern

Prevention: Balance training exercises daily, home safety evaluation, proper footwear, hip strengthening focus

Hip Labral Tear

  • Right hip ROM limitations and positive FABER test
